scope: Static review plus VM execution of frozen collector against synthetic in-memory fs/AWS; no real filesystem artifacts read through collector, cloud calls, Docker builds or launches.

reproductions.name: stale cached PASS for different source
cached FAILED exits as successful process

findings.problem: Cached readback is returned before source/start/template/log verification, so mismatched source proof can be returned for current candidate. Every cached result uses process.exit(0), including FAILED.
findings.repair: Validate cached service/source/build ID/buildspec/candidate/checkpoint/log bindings after local start/template checks. Require accepted qualification/status shape, and exit nonzero for FAILED. Preserve explicit reconciliation for incomplete log/readback writes.

passingChecks: Start checks exact source SHA, clean HEAD and current GitHub main.
Start requires qualification checkpoint bytes, review hash, template-checks hash, exact template bytes and sourcePins. Final candidate/checkpoint data still pending separate validation.
Exact account/user/GitHub source/ARM/privileged project and candidate tag absence are checked before any mutation.
Fixed per-service root, atomic mkdir and wx writes prevent reuse. Launch intent and full request with random idempotency token exist before start-build.

Only start-build uses awsSingleAttempt; it forces AWS_MAX_ATTEMPTS=1 and AWS_RETRY_MODE=standard, has one bounded CLI invocation, and exposes no automatic retry. Unknown result writes failure and prior root blocks rerun.
Fresh collector verifies exact source/resolved source/project/buildspec/env, SUCCEEDED, line-exact required markers, >=1570 orchestrator tests/130 suites/2 skips, and immutable ECR digest echo.
No Actions dispatch, production deployment, database, schedule, provider or live-capture call in these operators.
limitations: No build launched; candidate/qualification JSON do not exist yet.
Local candidate pins and request-input/intent lineage must be rechecked after source freeze.
Cloud project source/environment checks and ECR publication are only performed by root authorized later; this audit does not attest current cloud state.
